text: Meridian Fabrication just failed its annual third-party security audit. The report lands with three findings, and none of them are theoretical — they're the three ways real companies actually fail audits, over and over, and every one maps directly to a chapter this course already covered in detail.

First, several servers across both operating systems are more than ninety days behind on patches, some with known critical vulnerabilities. Second, a GPO applied domain-wide grants local Administrator rights to a group far broader than it should, left over from an old project nobody cleaned up. Third, a Linux database server still allows root login and password authentication over SSH.

The patch fix starts with triage, not blanket installs. Severity gets prioritized by CVSS score, so a critical remote-code-execution flaw on an internet-facing box jumps the queue ahead of a low-severity issue on an isolated one. Every patched server gets a documented re-scan afterward, because a fix without proof is next year's finding again.

Finding the permissive GPO means pulling its actual report rather than guessing, then narrowing local Administrators membership back to the specific groups that need it. Finding three gets handled differently: before the SSH config even changes, the auth log and audit history get searched for root logins during however long that exposure window lasted.

That's the real distinction in this case study — a database server with root login and password auth both exposed isn't just a misconfiguration to quietly flip, it's treated as a possible compromise until the logs say otherwise. Every fix here, patch, GPO, and SSH alike, gets re-verified and re-scanned, not just applied and assumed.

Three findings, three fixes, and not one new concept required to close any of them — just this course's own material, applied under a real deadline with a report due back to the auditor and a reputation on the line. That's exactly what the final lesson pulls together next: every chapter in this course, in one last review.
